subject: storytime
title: The Crow and the Pitcher
about: Aesop's fable of the thirsty crow who cannot reach the water at the bottom of a pitcher, until she stops to think and drops in stones, one by one, to bring the water up. It shows first graders that a hard problem gets solved by thinking it through and sticking with it, and the trick really works, so they can try it at the kitchen table. It is a public-domain story retold here in first-grade words, four pages long.
tip: Try it: drop pebbles into a glass with a little water in it and watch the water climb, just like in the story.

book.author: Aesop (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: A thirsty crow, a tall pitcher, and one clever idea.

passage.text:
The sun was hot, and the land was dry.
A crow was very thirsty.
She flew and flew, looking for water.
At last she saw a pitcher.
There was some water in it!
But the water was down low.
She put her beak in.
She could not reach the water.
***
"I will tip it over," said the crow.
She pushed and pushed.
But the pitcher was too heavy.
It did not tip.
"I will break it," she said.
Peck, peck, peck!
But the pitcher was too strong.
It did not break.
The crow sat and thought.
***
Then she saw some little stones.
She had an idea!
She picked up a stone in her beak.
Plop!
She dropped it in the pitcher.
The water came up a little.
She dropped in one more stone.
Plop!
The water came up a little more.
***
Plop, plop, plop!
Stone after stone went in.
Bit by bit, the water came up.
At last it was at the top.
The crow drank and drank.
What a clever crow!
She did not give up.
Think it through, and keep on trying.

cards.note: Crows are some of the smartest birds, and real crows have solved this very puzzle in science tests.

cards.q: What did the crow find with water in it?
cards.note: There was water inside, but it was too far down for her beak to reach.

cards.q: What did the crow drop into the pitcher?
cards.note: Each stone takes up room at the bottom, so the water has to move up.

cards.q: What happened to the water each time a stone went in?
cards.note: Bit by bit, stone by stone, the water rose until it was at the top.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: She found the pitcher, tried to tip it, tried to break it, and only then thought of the stones.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: After all that work she finally got her drink, and she drank and drank.
The story calls her a clever crow, because she stopped, thought, and found a better way.
Pushing and pecking did not work, so she thought it through and kept going until it did.

cards.q: In the story, what is a 'pitcher'?
cards.note: A pitcher is a tall jug with a handle and a spout for pouring, like a lemonade jug.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
